skill.name: vercel-cli
skill.description: Guides deployment, configuration, and troubleshooting with the Vercel CLI. Use when operating Vercel projects or resources through the CLI, especially for workflows spanning multiple commands, including deployments, CI, build failures, logs, metrics, Speed Insights, traces, environment variables, domains and DNS, firewall and WAF rules, Global Config (Edge Config), feature flags, storage and Blob, Container Registry (VCR), microfrontends, Sandbox, and `vercel api` fallback.
skill.summary: Plan and troubleshoot Vercel CLI workflows with project targeting, credential handling, and deployment verification guidance.
skill.author: vercel

content.user_title: Manage Vercel Deployments and CLI Workflows
content.value_statement: Vercel operations can target the wrong project or confuse incomplete telemetry with successful execution. This skill guides scoped CLI workflows with credential safeguards and explicit verification.
actual_capabilities: Guide source, prebuilt, and redeployment workflows while preserving deployment identity through verification and promotion.
Explain local project links, repository mappings, and explicit project or team targeting.
Structure build investigations using deployment metadata, logs, source inputs, and cache evidence.
Guide bounded log, metric, and trace queries with pagination and coverage checks.
Explain environment pulls, secret redaction, Blob authentication precedence, and storage connection changes.
Select task-specific references and use installed CLI help or scoped API discovery for command details.
limitations: This skill provides workflow guidance, not a bundled Vercel CLI installation or authenticated account.
Available commands and output formats depend on the installed CLI version.
Telemetry access depends on permissions, subscription features, retention, and network reachability.
Authentication, purchases, and destructive operations can require user interaction or explicit authorization.

use_cases.title: Validate an Application Deployment
use_cases.description: Choose the correct source or prebuilt path, verify the target project, and check the deployment state before promotion.

use_cases.title: Investigate a Production Regression
use_cases.description: Inspect the supplied deployment, query the affected time window, and distinguish observed failures from telemetry gaps.

use_cases.title: Configure Monorepo Delivery
use_cases.description: Check repository mappings, align build and deployment environments, and verify artifact completeness across CI jobs.

prompt_templates.title: Check CLI Readiness
prompt_templates.prompt: Check the installed Vercel CLI and explain its help for inspecting a deployment. Do not install, upgrade, authenticate, or change resources.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: understand the available CLI without modifying the environment.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare a Preview Deployment
prompt_templates.prompt: Prepare a preview deployment from [app directory]. Verify the resolved team and project first. Explain the source choice and request approval before deploying.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: validate targeting and deployment inputs.

prompt_templates.title: Diagnose a Failed Deployment
prompt_templates.prompt: Investigate [deployment URL] during [time window]. Inspect metadata and build logs, then relevant telemetry. Separate proven causes from hypotheses. Do not mutate resources.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: perform an evidence-based deployment investigation.

prompt_templates.title: Review a Monorepo CI Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Review [app directory] for a split build/deploy CI workflow. Verify mappings, environment consistency, and artifact completeness. Propose changes without applying them or revealing credentials.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: assess cross-job delivery and project boundaries.

output_examples.input: Review my preview deployment plan before running it.
output: Target check: confirm the resolved team and project from the application working directory.
Source choice: use local source for checkout changes, or the prebuilt path for existing build output.
Verification: wait for Ready or Error before reporting completion.

output_examples.input: Does an empty log page prove that the incident did not happen?
output: No. Confirm the project, deployment, environment, and affected time window.
Check pagination and excluded intervals before drawing conclusions.
Distinguish missing data from permission, retention, and subscription limits.

output_examples.input: Why can a valid Blob token fail when local OIDC variables are present?
output: Partial OIDC configuration produces an error instead of falling back to the read-write token.
A complete OIDC pair takes precedence over a static token within the same environment source.
Check configuration completeness without printing credential values.

best_practices: Verify the resolved team, project, and environment before pulling data or changing resources.
Use installed CLI help, preserve the chosen version, and keep credentials out of arguments and output.
Check final deployment states, pagination, and telemetry coverage before reporting success or absence.
anti_patterns: Assuming an application directory name or successful login proves the intended project target.
Treating non-interactive mode, suggested commands, or API access as permission to mutate resources.
Disabling deployment protection or bypassing confirmation to work around access limitations.

faq.question: Does this skill include the Vercel CLI?
faq.answer: No. It guides CLI usage and prefers the installation and version already chosen by the project.

faq.question: Can I use it with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill supports these tools. Actual operations still require CLI access, appropriate credentials, and user authorization.

faq.question: How does it choose the correct monorepo project?
faq.answer: It checks the resolved project from the actual working directory and explains precedence between local links and repository mappings.

faq.question: Will an environment pull recover stored Secret values?
faq.answer: No. A redacted Secret preserves an existing local value or produces a placeholder. Obtain usable credentials from the appropriate secret owner.

faq.question: Can it diagnose missing logs?
faq.answer: It guides checks for target scope, time windows, pagination, excluded intervals, permissions, and retention. Missing telemetry does not prove healthy behavior.

faq.question: Will it automatically bypass interactive confirmations?
faq.answer: No. The guidance preserves authentication handoffs and operation-specific confirmation requirements. Non-interactive execution does not supply consent.
